stem: Silver sulfide, $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$, is very insoluble in water.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Write an expression for the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}(\text{s})$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The solubility of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}(\text{s})$ in water at $298\text{ K}$ is $1.16 \times 10^{-17}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

Calculate the numerical value of the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}(\text{s})$ at $298\text{ K}$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the minimum volume of water needed to dissolve $1.00\text{ g}$ of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}(\text{s})$ under standard conditions.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Bromic(I) acid, $\text{HOBr}(\text{aq})$, is a weak acid. Its $K_{\text{a}}$ is $2.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.
parts.text: Calculate the pH of $0.20\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HOBr}(\text{aq})$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
$5.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.20\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ potassium hydroxide, $\text{KOH}$, are added to $20.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.20\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HOBr}(\text{aq})$.

Calculate the pH of the buffer solution produced.
